name: Gloria Steinem
role: American feminist journalist and activist, co-founder of Ms. magazine (1934-2026)
summary: Steinem was a leading figure of second-wave American feminism who campaigned for the Equal Rights Amendment and reproductive freedom, argued that sexism and racism are intertwined, and backed Democratic candidates such as Hillary Clinton. She opposed pornography and the legalised sex trade, favouring the Nordic model, and supported legal recognition of same-sex couples and, after an earlier controversy, trans people.

abortion-legal.rationale: Campaigned for reproductive freedom; in her 2017 speech backed the right to decide whether and when to give birth without government interference; framed the question as who decides, a woman or the government.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In her 1970 essay on a future where women win she expected lesbians and gay men to be able to marry legally; she signed the 2006 'Beyond Same-Sex Marriage' statement, which wants broader recognition of relationships, not less.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: she anticipated legally binding marriages for gay and lesbian couples (1970) and said sexuality limited to reproduction harms gay men and lesbians (2004), which is incompatible with criminalising same-sex relations.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: As quoted by an abolitionist group, she called prostitution oppression, opposed legalising the sex trade and favoured the Nordic model, which fines buyers; this is opposed to making sex work legal.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Described patriarchal controls and patriarchy as shaping women's bodies and sexuality (and limiting men's too); her 2017 and 1971 speeches describe sex used to sort people into superior and inferior groups.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Said there is no defeating sexism without also being anti-racist and that sex and race have both been used to sort people and supply cheap labour; rejected 'white feminism'.

gender-social-construct.rationale: In her ERA testimony argued that women's supposed inferiority rests on myths, not biology, and later urged raising sons more like daughters; in 2013 spoke of a 'full human continuum of identity and expression'. She did not use the phrase in the statement.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: In 2013 said trans lives should be celebrated, not questioned, and backed the Employment Non-Discrimination Act; in 2020 opposed the Trump administration's rollback of trans health-care protections. Retracted her 1977 remarks.

women-suffrage.rationale: Campaigned for equal legal rights for women including the ERA and political participation, and remarked that Black men got the vote about half a century before women of any race.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Defined a feminist as someone who recognises the equality and full humanity of women and men.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Testified for the ERA against sex-based laws and 'protective' labour laws that hold women back, and argued sex roles are myths.

traditional-family.rationale: Told the Senate that the new family is an egalitarian family and argued the family changes with the economy, rather than treating traditional structures as the foundation of society.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Described an egalitarian family and said it is possible to make an equal marriage.

premarital-sex.rationale: In 1969 described a liberated woman as one who has sex before marriage and a job after it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: In 2004 named Bush's opposition to sex education among reasons she called him a danger to health and safety.

god-not-male.rationale: In a 2012 interview described spirituality as rejecting a god who looks like the ruling class; she did not directly address gendered language for God.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Called the 2017 march true democracy and called for deep democracy and people power; said lasting change comes from the bottom up.

direct-action.rationale: Said that sometimes people must put their bodies where their beliefs are and that winning elections is not enough, but she also campaigned for candidates; evidence points both ways.

defeat-communism.rationale: Worked for the Independent Research Service (1958-62), described by her as liberal, nonviolent and honorable, and regarded the agency as an ally against communism in the early Cold War; this is her one recorded stance on communism and it is context-bound.

gradual-change.rationale: Said of the women's movement in 1968 'This is no simple reform. It really is a revolution'; she did not address respect for institutions directly.

notes: Wikipedia gives her death as 2 September 2026 in Manhattan at age 92, so living is false (catalog said false). Her 1977 remarks on transgender surgery were retracted in 2013; the 2013 position is used. Not found in sources opened: her own words on economic policy, a national homemaker's salary, Israel/Palestine (she criticised Netanyahu in 2019 and condemned the 1975 UN Zionism resolution per secondary reports, not opened), Native American matriarchal societies, or the pay gap beyond her 1970 testimony. Books were not available as full text (archive.org lending locked), so many topics stay null. Pornography: she opposed it as domination but no source opened shows she backed legal restriction, so restrict-pornography is null.
